simple.meaning: גָּדֵר (gâdêr) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a circumvallation ; by implication, an inclosure.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 22:24. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּדֵר (H1447) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: גָּדֵר (gâdêr) / H1447 is traced through Numbers 22:24, Ezra 9:9, Psalms 62:4, Psalms 80:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Yahweh’s angel stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
Then Yahweh’s angel stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.

For we are bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to revive us, to set up the house of our God, and to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
They fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place.
The boar out of the wood ravages it.
He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard.
You have not gone up into the gaps or built up the wall for the house of Israel, to stand in the battle in Yahweh’s day.
“I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I would not destroy it; but I found no one.
The wall that was outside by the side of the rooms, toward the outer court before the rooms, its length was fifty cubits.
A day to build your walls—
